docs.title: 5. Backups & Business Continuity
docs.text:
1. Automated Backups:
  2. Full backups: Weekly.
  3. Differential backups: Every 12–24 hours.
  4. Transaction log backups: Every 5–10 minutes.
  5. Point-in-Time Restore (PITR):
  6. Restores a database to any point in time within the retention window.
  7. Default: 7 days (configurable from 1 to 35 days).
  8. Long-Term Retention (LTR):
  9. Stores full backups for regulatory compliance for up to 10 years using Azure Backup vault policies (W-M-Y: Weekly, Monthly, Yearly).
  10. Backup Storage Redundancy:
  11. Configurable independently of compute tier: LRS (local), ZRS (zone), GRS (geo-redundant, default), or GZRS.

docs.title: 6. Security, Encryption & Compliance
docs.text: Security Area Technology Implementation & Exam Details Identity & Access Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) Centralized identity management. Enables MFA, Conditional Access, and passwordless authentication via Managed Identities. Network Security Private Link / Private Endpoint Secures access over private IP within the VNet, blocking public internet exposure. Data at Rest Transparent Data Encryption (TDE) Encrypts database files, log files, and backups at rest using AES-256. Can use Service-Managed Keys or Customer-Managed Keys (BYOK via Azure Key Vault). Data in Transit TLS 1.2+ Enforces transport layer encryption between client applications and Azure SQL. Data in Use / Process Always Encrypted Client driver encrypts sensitive columns before transmitting to database. Database processes ciphertext and never accesses plaintext. With Secure Enclaves, cryptographic operations (like equality/range queries) can occur inside hardware enclaves. Data in Use Encryption Types Deterministic vs. Randomized • Deterministic: Always yields the same ciphertext for a given plaintext value; allows point lookups, joins, grouping, and indexing.• Randomized: Generates different ciphertext for identical plaintext; more secure, but prevents searching, grouping, and indexing. Presentation Layer Dynamic Data Masking (DDM) NOT encryption. Obfuscates sensitive data in query results (e.g. XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-1234 or custom masks) on the fly for non-privileged users without altering underlying data. Access Control Row-Level Security (RLS) Uses SQL predicate functions to restrict which rows a user can see based on user identity or role (e.g., tenants can only access rows matching their TenantID). Audit & Integrity Ledger for Azure SQL Provides cryptographic proof of data integrity using SHA-256 block hashing (tamper-evident tables and ledgers). Protects against unauthorized modifications even by high-privileged DBAs. Threat Protection Microsoft Defender for SQL Vulnerability assessments, anomalous activity detection, and SQL injection alerting.

docs.title: Recovery
docs.text:
Please see this note

  1. Always On availability groups: Primary VM sends copies of all committed transactions to at least one replica in the availability group. synchronous commit replication ensures zero data loss for synchronous replicas.
  2. Always On Failover Cluster Instance: uses Windows Server Failover Clustering (WSFC) to provide high availability for SQL Server instances. If the primary instance fails, a secondary instance automatically takes over.
  3. Multi-Region or Hybrid Always On availability groups: If the primary site fails, you can fail over to a secondary Availability Group in a different location, either within Azure or on-premises.
  4. Distributed availability groups: Provides high availability for SQL Server instances across multiple availability groups.
  5. Log shipping: Copy transaction log backups from a primary SQL Server to one or more secondary SQL Servers. The transaction log backups are restored on the secondary server, keeping it synchronized with the primary server.

docs.title: 3. Site-to-Site (S2S) VPN
docs.text: A Site-to-Site VPN connects an on-premises network to an Azure Virtual Network over an encrypted IPsec/IKE tunnel.

docs.title: Required Azure Components
docs.text:
1. Virtual Network (VNet): The target network in Azure.

  2. GatewaySubnet:

    • Must be named exactly GatewaySubnet.
    • Cannot contain workloads (VMs).
    • Recommended size: /27 or /28 (minimum /29).
    • Do NOT attach an NSG or UDR (with 0.0.0.0/0) that blocks gateway management traffic.
    • Virtual Network Gateway (VPN Gateway):

  3. Gateway Type: VPN (vs ExpressRoute).

  4. VPN Type: Route-based (recommended; supports IKEv2, P2S, BGP) vs Policy-based (legacy IKEv1, static IP ranges only).
  5. Public IP Address: Standard SKU (Zone-redundant for VpnGw#AZ SKUs).

  6. Local Network Gateway (LNG):

  7. Represents the on-premises VPN router/firewall in Azure.

  8. Defines: On-premises public IP (or FQDN) and on-premises IP address prefixes (CIDR).
  9. Contains on-prem BGP settings (ASN and BGP peer IP) if BGP is used.

  10. VPN Connection:

  11. The Azure resource that links the Virtual Network Gateway to the Local Network Gateway.

  12. Configures the Pre-Shared Key (PSK) and IPsec/IKE policy.

docs.title: 4. Point-to-Site (P2S) VPN
docs.text: Connects individual client devices (Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android) to an Azure VNet.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
• Configured directly on the Virtual Network Gateway under Point-to-site configuration.
  • Address Pool: Dedicated private IP range allocated to connected VPN clients (cannot overlap with VNet or on-premises ranges).

  • Protocols / Tunnels:

    • OpenVPN: Cross-platform (Windows, Mac, Linux, mobile); supports Entra ID auth.
    • SSTP: Secure Sockets Tunneling Protocol (Windows-only, TCP 443 — passes easily through firewalls/proxies).
    • IKEv2: Fast, standards-based mobile/desktop VPN.
    • Authentication Methods:

  • Azure Certificate Authentication: Root certificate uploaded to Azure; client certificate installed on user machine.

  • Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD): Modern user-based auth (MFA, Conditional Access). Requires OpenVPN tunnel and Azure VPN Client app.
  • RADIUS Authentication: Integrates with on-premises Active Directory via Network Policy Server (NPS).

docs.title: 6. ExpressRoute & Coexistence
docs.text:
1. ExpressRoute:

    • Dedicated private connection via a Connectivity Partner (MPLS, Ethernet, or Cloud Exchange).
    • Does not travel over the public Internet.
    • Uses BGP for dynamic routing.

    • ExpressRoute + VPN Gateway Coexistence (Failover):

    • Both an ExpressRoute Gateway and a Route-Based VPN Gateway can coexist in the same GatewaySubnet.

    • The S2S VPN tunnel acts as a backup / failover if the ExpressRoute circuit fails.
    • By default, traffic prefers ExpressRoute over the VPN connection because ExpressRoute BGP routes are shorter/preferred.
